question: 该不该信命？
sub: 算命、八字、星座为何长盛不衰——是迷信、逃避，还是一面照见自己的镜子？
sub_en: Why fortune-telling and astrology endure — superstition, evasion, or a mirror that shows you yourself?

casting.reason: 他把这道题拆成两句话：天有它的常轨，不因谁的祈求而改；卜筮祭祷这类事，君子当它是礼的装饰，百姓当它是神的意旨——同一套仪节，两种态度，吉凶就分在这里。他不主张废掉求签祭祀，那些仪式自有安顿人心、维系人群的用处；他反对的是把它当成因果。人真正能做的是把天当作可以了解、可以取用的东西，而不是仰头思慕它。在他看来，唯一靠得住的改命之法是学与积——今天多学一分，明天的处境就真的不同一分。
casting.reason_en: He splits the question into two sentences. Heaven runs on constant courses and does not alter them for anyone's prayers; and rites like divination and sacrifice are ornament in the eyes of the gentleman but the will of spirits in the eyes of the crowd — one and the same ceremony, two attitudes, and that is where fortune and disaster part. He does not want the temple queues abolished: such rites genuinely settle troubled minds and hold a community together. What he refuses is treating them as causes. What a person can actually do is treat heaven as something to be understood and put to use rather than gazed at in longing, and the only reliable way to change a life is study and accumulation — learn one more thing today and tomorrow's situation is genuinely different by that much.

casting.reason: 在他看来，星盘从来不是天体在推人，而是一面投射的镜子；那些流传数千年的符号，是心灵自身的结构在外部找到的形状。他给来访者排过星盘，用作进入无意识的入口，看重的不是预言准不准，而是人被说中时身上起的那点反应——那说明有些东西早就在那里，只是一直没被承认。他也划下了界线：一旦把镜子当成命令，个体化的历程就停了，人把自己的选择外包给了一张图。他要保住的是象征的用处，同时不让它变成权威。
casting.reason_en: For him a birth chart is never the planets pushing anyone around; it is a mirror for projection, and symbols that have circulated for millennia are the structure of the psyche finding an outward shape. He cast charts for the people who came to him, using them as an entrance to the unconscious, and what mattered was never predictive accuracy but the small jolt in someone who has just been described accurately — evidence that something was already there and had gone unacknowledged. He also draws a line: the moment the mirror is taken for an order, individuation stops and the person has outsourced their own choices to a diagram. He wants to keep the usefulness of symbols without letting them become an authority.

casting.reason: 他把分歧立到最硬处：人没有预先写好的本质，只有他做过的事的总和；说一句『我这人天生如此』就是自欺——把自己说成一件被规定好的东西，好让选择显得不必署名。他不认为信命首先是知识问题，而是伦理问题：一张出生表之所以被搬出来，是因为它替人挡掉了那句『这是我选的』。他承认这份自由是重负，人是被判处自由的，逃不掉也退不回；但他不肯发给任何人一张放下重负的许可证。
casting.reason_en: He sets the disagreement at its hardest point: a person has no essence written in advance, only the sum of what they have done, and the sentence 'that's just how I am' is bad faith — recasting yourself as a thing already specified so that your choices need not be signed. Believing in fate is not, to him, primarily a question of knowledge but of ethics: a birth chart gets produced precisely because it deflects the sentence 'I chose this.' He grants that such freedom is a burden — we are condemned to be free, with no way out and no way back — but he will issue nobody a permit to set the burden down.

casting.reason: 这套区分是从奴隶的处境里长出来的：有些事由我，有些事不由我，而痛苦几乎全部来自把不由我的事当成由我的。占卜师能说外面将要发生什么，却说不了那件事对你是好是坏——那个判断永远留在你手里，谁也拿不走。他还有更硬的一条：凡属本分之事不必问卦，朋友有难该不该救、许过的话该不该守，去问神就已经是在找退路。所以他既不拦着人去问，也不允许把问来的答案当成行动的理由。
casting.reason_en: The distinction grew out of a slave's situation: some things are up to me, some are not, and nearly all suffering comes from treating what is not up to me as if it were. A diviner can tell you what will happen outside you but never whether it is good or bad for you — that verdict stays in your hands and nobody can take it. He holds a harder line too: what duty already settles needs no oracle. Whether to help a friend in danger, whether to keep a promise you made — going to consult the gods about that is already looking for a way out. So he neither stops anyone from asking nor lets the answer count as a reason for acting.

casting.reason: 他不站在信与不信任何一边，先把宿命论从因果里拆出来：倘若此刻的苦乐全由前世注定，那么修与不修都无意义，善恶也无处着落——这种主张他列为外道，从不认领。业不是一本写好的账簿，而是仍在起作用的因缘；条件变了，果就跟着变，所以人当下所做的事仍然算数。面对正在受苦的人，他更愿意先拔箭：箭从哪儿来、谁射的、材质如何，都可以之后再问，眼下第一件事是止痛。
casting.reason_en: He takes neither the believing nor the disbelieving side, and begins by prising fatalism apart from causation. If every pleasure and pain in this moment were fixed by past lives, then practising or not practising would make no difference and good and evil would have nowhere to land — a view he lists among the outsiders' doctrines and never claims. Karma is not a ledger already written but conditions still at work: change the conditions and the result changes, so what a person does now still counts. Faced with someone in pain he would rather draw the arrow first — where it came from, who shot it, what it is made of can all be asked later; the first task is to stop the bleeding.

casting.reason: 他把这件事拉回可观察的地方。1948 年他让鸽子在与行为毫无关系的固定间隔里得食，鸽子却各自练出一套转圈、抬头、蹭墙的『仪式』——奖赏与动作偶然相邻一次，足以造出迷信，全程不需要任何信念参与。人也一样：那句碰巧算准的话、那次戴了红绳恰好顺利的经历，都在悄悄强化后面的行为。所以他不主张跟人辩论星座真假，主张换掉强化：与其争论命存不存在，不如把偶然与结果之间的账当场记清楚。
casting.reason_en: He drags the matter back to what can be observed. In 1948 he fed pigeons on a fixed interval that had nothing to do with their behaviour, and the birds each drilled up a private 'ritual' — turning circles, bobbing, brushing a wall. One accidental pairing of reward with movement is enough to manufacture superstition, and no belief is required anywhere in the process. People work the same way: the reading that happened to land, the day the red string was on your wrist and things went well, quietly reinforce whatever came before them. So he has no interest in arguing about whether astrology is true; he wants the reinforcement changed. Rather than debate whether fate exists, keep an honest ledger of what coincidence actually paid out.

casting.reason: 他研究过一个笃信世界末日的小团体：预言落空的那个夜里，信徒不但没有散去，反而第一次开始向外传教。由此他得出一条冷峻的结论——信念与事实冲突时，人宁可扭曲信念，尤其在已经付出昂贵代价之后。这解释了这道题里最反直觉的一半：算不准并不动摇信，有时反而加固信。他还提醒，人在缺乏客观标准时会拿他人当尺子来评估自己，而一套命理提供的恰恰是一把现成、随时可用、还不会还嘴的尺。
casting.reason_en: He studied a small group convinced the world was about to end, and on the night the prophecy failed the believers did not disperse — they began, for the first time, to proselytise. From that he drew a bleak conclusion: when belief and fact collide, people would rather distort the belief, especially once they have paid dearly for it. This accounts for the most counter-intuitive half of the question — being wrong does not shake such systems and can even strengthen them. He adds that people lacking an objective standard measure themselves against others, and a fate system offers exactly that: a ready-made yardstick, available at any hour, that never answers back.

casting.reason: 他关心的是『为何长盛不衰』这半句。现代化的核心是祛魅：世界不再有神秘莫测的力量，凡事原则上都能计算——可科学恰恰答不了『我该怎么活』这一问。空缺留在那里，就会被重新填上，只是这一次填进去的形式是可消费的、没有教会、也不要求任何义务。他还带来一个现成的反例：加尔文派把一切判定为神早已拣选，结果不是信众躺下等着，而是把劳动做成确证自己得救的方式，反倒催出了最勤勉的一代人。
casting.reason_en: His interest is in the second half of the question: why these things endure. Modernity's core process is disenchantment — no more incalculable forces, everything in principle masterable by reckoning — and yet science is precisely what cannot answer the question of how one ought to live. A vacancy like that gets refilled, and this time the filling is consumable, has no church and demands no obligations. He also brings a ready counter-example: Calvinism declared everything settled by God's election, and the result was not believers lying down to wait but labour turned into a way of confirming one's own salvation, which produced the most industrious generation on record.

casting.reason: 她要问的是这句『命该如此』由谁说出、说给谁听、说完之后谁省了事。她一生的工作是揭穿一件事：被称作天生的东西，多半是历史与权力造出来的，女人不是天生的，是被塑造成的。命理最常见的用途从来不是解释宇宙，而是给一个已经安排好的位置盖一个自然的章。但她同样不肯说『你完全自由』——自由永远在处境中展开，对一个手里没有任何资源可调动的人，这句轻飘飘的话本身就是一种残忍。
casting.reason_en: Her question is who says 'that is simply your lot', to whom, and who is spared trouble once it has been said. Her life's work was to expose one thing: what gets called natural is usually the product of history and power — one is not born a woman, one becomes one. The commonest use of a fate system was never to explain the cosmos but to stamp a position already assigned to someone as natural. She refuses the opposite slogan just as firmly: nobody is simply free. Freedom always unfolds inside a situation, and to a person with no resources to move, the airy line about being free is itself a cruelty.

casting.reason: 他关心谁承担后果。人受不了随机，于是给噪音配上故事，把活下来的那几个当作证据，全然忘了没算准的从不出现在样本里。他的判据简单粗暴：任何对你的人生发言、却不承担一丝后果的人，说的都不算预测。他也不主张全盘扫荡——花两百块买个安心，和把八字写进一个不可逆的决定，是完全不同的两件事：前者是消费，后者是把方向盘交给一个不坐在车上的人，而车祸只由你自己赔。
casting.reason_en: What interests him is who bears the consequences. People cannot tolerate randomness, so they fit stories to noise, take the few survivors as evidence and forget that the readings which missed never enter the sample at all. His test is blunt: anyone who pronounces on your life while bearing none of the downside is not making a prediction. He is not out to abolish the whole trade either — paying a small fee for peace of mind and writing a horoscope into an irreversible decision are entirely different acts. The first is consumption; the second hands the wheel to someone who is not in the car, while the crash is billed to you alone.

posts.text: 先说一个不需要任何神秘的实验。一九四八年，我把鸽子关进箱子，每隔十五秒落一次食，落不落跟它当时在做什么毫无关系。八只鸽子有六只很快练出了自己的一套动作：有的逆时针转圈，有的反复把头抬向箱角，有的蹭墙。它们把偶然相邻的动作当成了原因，我称之为迷信行为。**造出一套迷信不需要谁相信什么，只需要一次凑巧的奖赏。**人比鸽子多的只是一张嘴——多出一套解释，说那是水星、是八字、是手上那根红绳。所以别急着问命存不存在，先问：上次算准之后，你的哪一个行为被强化了？
posts.text_en: Let me open with an experiment that needs no mystery at all. In 1948 I put pigeons in a box and delivered food every fifteen seconds regardless of what the bird happened to be doing. Six of the eight quickly drilled up a routine of their own: one turned counter-clockwise, one kept tossing its head toward a corner, one brushed against the wall. They had taken an accidental adjacency for a cause, and I called it superstitious behaviour. **Manufacturing a superstition requires nobody to believe anything; it requires one well-timed reward.** All a human has that a pigeon lacks is a mouth — an extra layer of explanation about Mercury, or the eight characters of a birth hour, or the red string on your wrist. So before asking whether fate exists, ask this: after the last reading that came true, which of your behaviours got reinforced?

glossary.迷信行为: superstitious behaviour（迷信行为）：斯金纳 1948 年提出的说法，指奖赏与行为无关地按时到来时，动物仍会把当时碰巧在做的动作当成原因，并反复重演它。它说明一套仪式的形成不需要任何信念或理解，只需要奖赏与动作在时间上碰巧挨在一起。
glossary.强化: reinforcement（强化）：某个行为之后出现的结果，使该行为将来更可能重复出现的过程。强化不要求当事人察觉，也不追问结果与行为之间是否真有因果——只要在时间上足够接近，行为就会被塑造。

glossary_en.superstitious behaviour: Skinner's 1948 term for what happens when a reward arrives on schedule regardless of behaviour: the animal treats whatever it happened to be doing as the cause and repeats it. It shows that a ritual needs no belief or understanding to form — only an accidental adjacency in time between action and reward.
glossary_en.reinforced: From reinforcement: a consequence following a behaviour that makes the behaviour more likely to recur. It requires no awareness in the subject and asks nothing about whether the consequence was genuinely caused by the act; closeness in time is enough to shape what a body does.

posts.text: 我给来访者排过星盘，也知道同行会为此皱眉。但我关心的从来不是天体的作用力。**一张星盘说不出将要发生什么，它只能让你听见你早已知道、却始终不肯承认的那部分。**一个人被说中时脸上那一下松动，远比预言本身重要：被承认的东西才有机会被整合，没被承认的会从背后驱使你。我用共时性称呼那些有意义的巧合——它不是因果，是意义在时间里的排布。那些流传了几千年的符号也不是天上写好的，是心灵自身的结构在外面找到的形状，我称之为原型。可我同样划一条线：一旦把镜子当成命令，人的个体化就停在那儿了。
posts.text_en: I cast charts for the people who came to me, and I know colleagues wince at it. But the force of the planets was never my concern. **A chart cannot tell you what will happen; it can only let you hear the part of yourself you already knew and have refused to admit.** The small loosening in someone's face when a description lands matters far more than any prediction: what is acknowledged has a chance of being integrated, and what is not drives you from behind. I use synchronicity for meaningful coincidence — not causation, but an arrangement of meaning in time. Nor were those symbols, circulating for thousands of years, written in the sky; they are the structure of the psyche finding an outward shape, and I call them archetypes. Still I draw a line: the moment the mirror is taken for an order, a person's individuation stops there.

glossary.共时性: synchronicity（共时性）：荣格用来描述『有意义的巧合』的术语——两件事之间没有可查的因果联系，却在当事人心里构成一个明确的意义整体。荣格拿它解释占卜、梦兆一类经验，同时承认它无法被实验证实，只能从当事人的体验里描述。
glossary.原型: archetype（原型）：荣格设想的、人类共有的心理模式——母亲、英雄、阴影、智慧老人之类反复出现在神话、宗教与梦里的形象。他认为具体内容因文化而异，产生这些形象的心理结构却是共通的。

glossary_en.synchronicity: Jung's term for meaningful coincidence: two events with no traceable causal link that nonetheless form one clear unit of meaning for the person living them. He used it to account for experiences of divination and omens while conceding it cannot be established experimentally, only described from the inside.
glossary_en.archetypes: Jung's name for shared human psychic patterns — mother, hero, shadow, wise old man — recurring across myth, religion and dreams. The content varies with culture, he held, while the structure producing the images is common to everyone.

posts.text: 天行有常，不为尧存，不为桀亡。日月星辰之行，其常也。雩而雨，何也？曰：无何也，犹不雩而雨也。卜筮然后决大事，非以为得求也，以文之也。故**君子以为文，而百姓以为神。以为文则吉，以为神则凶。**大天而思之，孰与物畜而制之？从天而颂之，孰与制天命而用之？故君子敬其在己者，而不慕其在天者；小人错其在己者，而慕其在天者。是以日进、日退之分也。
posts.text_en: Heaven runs on constant courses. It did not persist because Yao ruled well, and it did not perish because Jie ruled badly; the movements of sun, moon and stars are simply its regularity. You perform the rain sacrifice and rain comes — why? For no reason at all. It rains just the same when nobody performs it. We consult the shell and the stalks before great decisions not because that obtains what we ask for, but to give the decision its proper form. **So the gentleman treats these rites as form, while the common people take them for spirits. Treat them as form and it goes well; take them for spirits and it goes badly.** To exalt Heaven and long for it — how does that compare with tending it as one tends a herd, and putting it to use? The gentleman reveres what lies within himself and does not yearn after what lies with Heaven; the small man neglects what lies within himself and yearns after Heaven. That is the whole difference between advancing daily and slipping daily.
posts.vernacular: 天的运行有它固定的常轨，不会因为尧是明君就多留一天，也不会因为桀是暴君就提前收摊；日月星辰照常走，这就是它的常。求雨的祭祀做完，雨下来了，是什么缘故？没有什么缘故——不做祭祀，该下的雨照样下。大事之前占卜问卦，并不是真能求来什么，只是让这件事有个郑重的形式。所以**君子把这些仪式当作礼的形式，百姓却把它当作神灵在显灵。当形式看待就吉利，当神明看待就凶险。**与其抬头思慕上天，不如把它当作可以了解、可以取用的东西；与其顺着天颂扬它，不如摸清它的规律去用它。君子看重的是自己手里那份，不去羡慕天上那份；小人放着自己手里那份不管，一心指望天上。一个天天往前，一个天天往后，分别就在这里。

glossary.制天命而用之: mastering the mandate of heaven and putting it to use（制天命而用之）：荀子《天论》里的主张——与其把天当作要顺从、要祈求的意志，不如把它当作有规律、可被认识、可被利用的自然过程。这一句常被视为先秦思想里最接近『征服自然』的表述，但荀子的重点在于人事：把注意力从祈求转回到耕作、储备与制度上。
glossary.雩: yu, the rain sacrifice（雩）：古代求雨的祭典，由官府主持，规模盛大。荀子拿它当例子：仪式与降雨之间没有因果关系，但仪式本身在安顿人心、组织人群上有实实在在的用处——他要区分的正是这两种『有用』。

glossary_en.putting it to use: From Xunzi's Discourse on Heaven: rather than treating heaven as a will to be obeyed and petitioned, treat it as a regular natural process that can be known and used. The line is often read as the closest thing in early Chinese thought to a call to master nature, though Xunzi's emphasis falls on human affairs — moving attention off petition and back onto farming, storage and institutions.
glossary_en.the rain sacrifice: A large state-sponsored ceremony for summoning rain. Xunzi uses it as his example: there is no causal link between the rite and the rainfall, yet the rite really does settle people and organise them. Distinguishing those two kinds of usefulness is precisely his point.

posts.text: 我要说的与准不准无关。就算星象真有那么一点统计上的影子，也改变不了这件事的性质。**你不是被算出来的，你是你做过的事的总和；而这个总和每天都还在被你自己追加。**『我天蝎座所以记仇』『我这就是劳碌命』——这类句子的功能从来不是描述，是免责。人拿一张出生表把自己变成一件被规定好的东西，好让选择显得不必署名，这就是自欺。请注意它有多舒服：命既解释了你昨天的失败，又预支了你明天的放弃。可签字的那只手一直是你自己的。人被判处自由，判决不接受上诉，也没有哪张星盘可以代你去领。
posts.text_en: What I have to say has nothing to do with accuracy. Even if the stars cast some faint statistical shadow, the nature of the act would not change. **You are not calculated; you are the sum of what you have done — and that sum is still being added to by you, daily.** 'I'm a Scorpio, that's why I hold grudges.' 'I was simply born to toil.' Sentences like these never function as descriptions; they function as waivers. A person uses a birth chart to turn himself into a thing already specified, so that his choices need not be signed, and that is bad faith. Notice how comfortable it is: fate explains yesterday's failure and advances you tomorrow's surrender in the same breath. But the hand doing the signing has been yours all along. We are condemned to be free; the sentence permits no appeal, and no chart can collect it on your behalf.

glossary.自欺: mauvaise foi / bad faith（自欺）：萨特用来指人对自己撒的一种特殊的谎——不是不知道真相，而是一边知道一边装作不知道，好把『我选择了』说成『我只能如此』。典型形式是把自己描述成一件有固定性质的东西（我天生怯懦、我命该如此），从而免去承担选择的责任。

glossary_en.bad faith: Sartre's name for a peculiar lie one tells oneself: not ignorance of the truth but knowing and simultaneously pretending not to, so that 'I chose this' can be restated as 'I could not do otherwise.' Its classic form is describing yourself as a thing with fixed properties — born timid, born to this lot — and thereby escaping responsibility for choosing.

posts.text: 先解释一件事：为什么在识字率、医疗与科学最发达的社会里，星座反而卖得最好。现代化的核心过程我称之为祛魅——世上不再有神秘莫测的力量，凡事原则上都可以计算。可科学能告诉你病毒如何传播，答不了你该怎么活；它撤走了意义的旧供应商，没有派来新的。**空出来的位置从不空着，只是这一回填进去的东西可以消费、没有教会、也不要求你尽任何义务。**再纠正一个流行的推论：加尔文派的预定论宣布救恩早已拣选、人力无从更改，结果不是信徒躺平等着，而是把劳动做成确证自己得救的凭据。所以信命究竟让人躺下还是让人拼命，全看这套命理配了什么行动指令。
posts.text_en: Something else needs explaining first: why horoscopes sell best in the societies with the highest literacy, the best medicine and the most science. The core process of modernity I call disenchantment — no more incalculable forces, everything in principle masterable by reckoning. Yet science, which can tell you how a virus spreads, cannot tell you how to live; it withdrew meaning's old supplier without sending a new one. **A vacancy like that never stays empty. It is only that this time the filling is consumable, has no church, and asks no duties of you.** And let me correct a popular inference. Calvinist predestination announced that salvation was settled by election and no human effort could alter it — whereupon believers did not lie down to wait, but turned labour into a way of confirming their own election. Whether belief in fate makes people slack or makes them drive themselves depends entirely on what instructions for action the system comes packaged with.

glossary.祛魅: disenchantment（祛魅）：韦伯用来概括现代化的核心过程——人们不再相信世上存在神秘莫测、须靠祈祷与法术打交道的力量，转而相信凡事原则上都可以通过计算与技术掌握。代价是意义问题被逐出了知识的范围：科学能回答『世界如何运作』，却答不了『我该怎么活』。
glossary.预定论: predestination（预定论）：加尔文派的核心教义，认为谁得救、谁不得救全由神在创世之前已经拣选，任何善功都无法更改。韦伯的著名论证是：这种教义带来的不是消极，而是极度的焦虑，信徒于是把职业上的成功当作自己蒙拣选的凭据，反倒催生出高度自律的劳动伦理。

glossary_en.disenchantment: Weber's summary of modernity's core process: people cease to believe in mysterious powers that must be handled by prayer and magic, and come to believe instead that everything can in principle be mastered by calculation and technique. The price is that questions of meaning are expelled from the domain of knowledge — science answers how the world works, never how one should live.
glossary_en.predestination: The central Calvinist doctrine that who is saved and who is not was settled by God before the creation and no good works can alter it. Weber's famous argument is that such a doctrine produced not passivity but acute anxiety, so that believers took worldly success in a calling as evidence of their own election — which in turn generated an extraordinarily disciplined work ethic.

posts.text: 有沙门婆罗门作如是说：人所受苦乐，皆由宿命所造。我不与之同。若一切苦乐悉由宿作，则杀盗淫妄亦宿作所使，何者为善？何者为恶？修与不修，等无所益。是名宿作因论，外道之说，我不摄受。业非已成之簿，乃现前之缘；缘转则果转，故今日所作，仍然有力。**若人中毒箭，当先拔箭；箭从何来、何人所射、其翎何色，皆可后问。**汝问命乎？先视苦之所起、苦之所灭：此可知、可证、可行，不待星辰之验。
posts.text_en: There are ascetics and brahmins who teach this: whatever a person feels, pleasant or painful, was all determined by past deeds. I do not agree with them. For if every pleasure and pain were fixed by what was done before, then killing, theft, lechery and lying would also be driven by what was done before — and what then would be good, what would be evil? Practice and non-practice would come to the same nothing. This is the doctrine of past-action determinism, a teaching of the outsiders, and I do not take it up. Karma is not a ledger already closed but conditions still at work: change the conditions and the fruit changes, so what you do today still has force. **If a man is struck by a poisoned arrow, draw the arrow first. Where it came from, who shot it, what colour its fletching was — all of that can be asked afterwards.** You ask about fate? Look first at how suffering arises and how it ceases. That much can be known, tested and practised, and it waits on no star.
posts.vernacular: 有些修行人和婆罗门这样讲：一个人所感受的苦与乐，全都由前世造下的业决定。我不同意。假如一切苦乐都由前世注定，那么杀生、偷盗、邪淫、妄语也都是前世驱使的了——那还有什么算善、什么算恶？修行与不修行也就毫无分别。这种主张叫宿作因论，是外道的说法，我从不接受。业不是一本已经写好、只等兑现的账簿，而是此刻仍在起作用的条件；条件变了，结果就跟着变，所以你今天做的事仍然算数。**一个人中了毒箭，第一件事是把箭拔出来；箭从哪儿来、谁射的、箭羽是什么颜色，都可以之后再问。**你问命吗？先看苦是怎么生起的、又是怎么止息的——这件事可以知道、可以验证、可以当下就做，用不着等星象来印证。

glossary.宿作因论: pubbekatahetu-vāda / past-action determinism（宿作因论）：主张人当下的一切苦乐全由前世所作决定的学说。佛陀把它与『一切由神所造』『一切无因无缘』并列为三种外道见，理由是：若苦乐全为前定，善恶便无从分辨，修行也失去意义——这正是佛教的因果观与宿命论的分界线。
glossary.业: karma（业）：意为『行为』，指身、口、意所造的行动及其后续影响。在佛教里业是仍在流动的条件，而非注定的判决：过去的行为塑造了当下的处境，当下的行为又参与塑造往后的处境，因此改变随时可能发生。

glossary_en.past-action determinism: Pubbekatahetu-vāda, the doctrine that everything one now feels was settled by deeds in past lives. The Buddha lists it, together with 'all is made by a god' and 'all is without cause', as one of three outsider views, on the grounds that if pleasure and pain are wholly predetermined then good and evil cannot be told apart and practice loses its point — which is exactly where Buddhist causation parts company with fatalism.
glossary_en.Karma: Literally 'action': what is done in body, speech and mind, together with its continuing effects. In Buddhism karma is a set of conditions still in motion rather than a verdict already passed — past action shaped the present situation, present action helps shape what follows, and so change remains possible at any moment.

posts.text: 一九五四年，我和同事以参与观察的方式混进一个笃信洪水将至的小团体。预言之夜，飞碟没来，洪水也没来。按常理他们该醒了，那天凌晨发生的却正相反：这群此前避不见人的信徒，第一次主动给报社打电话、上街传教。这个机制我称为认知失调——信念与事实撞车时，扭曲信念远比承认错误便宜，而已经付出的代价越大，扭曲得越用力。**所以一套命理长盛不衰，往往不是因为它常常应验，而是因为它落空时你已经赔不起了。**辞了工作、退了婚、把积蓄捐出去的那几个人，恰恰是最不可能承认那晚什么都没发生的人。
posts.text_en: In 1954 a colleague and I embedded ourselves, as participant observation demands, in a small group convinced a flood was coming. On the appointed night no saucer came and no flood came. By common sense they should have woken up; what happened in the small hours was the reverse. Believers who had until then avoided outsiders began, for the first time, phoning newspapers and preaching in the street. I call the mechanism cognitive dissonance: when belief collides with fact, bending the belief is far cheaper than admitting the error, and the more you have already paid, the harder you bend. **So a fate system endures not because it is often right, but because when it fails you can no longer afford to have been wrong.** The few who had quit jobs, broken off engagements and given away their savings were precisely the ones least able to concede that nothing had happened that night.

glossary.认知失调: cognitive dissonance（认知失调）：费斯廷格提出的理论，指人同时持有两个互相冲突的认知（如『我很理性』与『我为一个落空的预言散尽家财』）时产生的不适，以及为消除这份不适而做的调整。关键在于：调整往往落在更容易改动的那一头——不是改行为，而是改对事实的解释。
glossary.参与观察: participant observation（参与观察）：社会科学的一种研究方法，研究者以成员身份进入所研究的群体，长期从内部观察其日常运作。它能拿到问卷问不出来的东西，代价是研究者的在场本身可能改变群体，因而至今仍有伦理争议。

glossary_en.cognitive dissonance: Festinger's theory of the discomfort produced by holding two conflicting cognitions at once — 'I am a rational person' and 'I gave away everything for a prophecy that failed' — and of the adjustments made to remove it. The crucial point is where the adjustment lands: usually on whichever side is easier to move, which means the account of the facts rather than the behaviour.
glossary_en.participant observation: A research method in which the investigator enters the group under study as a member and watches its daily workings from inside over a long period. It yields what no questionnaire can, at the cost that the researcher's presence may itself change the group — which is why it remains ethically contested.

posts.text: 先别问命准不准，问一句：这句『你就是这个命』通常由谁说出口，说给谁听，说完之后谁省了事。我一生只证明了一件事：被称作天生的，多半是历史造出来、再被说成自然的。女人不是天生的，是被塑造成的；每个时代都需要一套说辞，把安排好的位置盖上一枚自然的印章。八字、血型、星座都能干这个活，而且比命令温柔得多：**你不必被押着，你自己认了，压迫就省下了一名看守。**被划到他者位置上的人，往往最早学会用命来解释自己的处境。但我不肯说出那句轻飘飘的反面：自由永远在处境里展开，对一个没钱、没假期、没有人可投奔的人，说『一切都是你的选择』同样是残忍。
posts.text_en: Before asking whether the readings are accurate, ask this: who usually says 'that is simply your lot', to whom, and who is spared trouble once it has been said. My life's work established one thing — what gets called natural is mostly made by history and then described as nature. One is not born a woman, one becomes one; and every age needs a formula for stamping an already assigned position as natural. Birth hours, blood types, star signs all do the job, and far more gently than an order does. **You need not be held down. Once you agree, the oppression has saved itself a guard.** Those consigned to the position of the Other are usually the first to learn to explain their situation by fate. Yet I refuse the airy opposite as well: freedom always unfolds inside a situation, and to someone with no money, no leave and nobody to fall back on, 'it is all your choice' is its own cruelty.

glossary.处境: situation（处境）：存在主义用语，指一个人做选择时所处的具体条件——身体、阶级、性别、时代、手上有多少钱与时间。波伏娃用它修正萨特式的『绝对自由』：自由是真的，但它永远在给定条件里施展，条件不同，同一个『选择』的代价可以相差十倍。
glossary.他者: the Other（他者）：波伏娃在《第二性》里的核心概念。一个群体把自己确立为标准的『主体』，另一群体便被定义为相对于它的、被观看被解释的一方。被置于他者位置的人，往往用统治者的语言来理解自己，于是不平等看上去像是天性使然。

glossary_en.situation: An existentialist term for the concrete conditions in which a person chooses: body, class, gender, era, how much money and time is actually in hand. Beauvoir used it to correct Sartre's absolute freedom — freedom is real, but it is always exercised inside given conditions, and the same 'choice' can cost ten times more depending on them.
glossary_en.the Other: Beauvoir's central concept in The Second Sex. One group establishes itself as the standard subject, and the other is thereby defined as the party that is looked at and explained. Those placed in that position tend to understand themselves in the dominant group's language, which makes the inequality look like a fact of nature.

posts.text: 我是奴隶出身，腿是被打瘸的，所以我对『什么由我』这件事没有任何浪漫想法。天下的事只分两类：由我的——判断、意愿、取舍；不由我的——身体、财产、名声、别人怎么想。这就是我的控制二分法。占卜师能说外面将要发生什么，却说不了那件事对你是好是坏，**因为好坏不在事情里，在你对它的判断里，而判断谁也拿不走。**还有更硬的一条：本分之事不必问卦。朋友有难该不该帮，许下的话该不该守，你若还要去问神，其实已经在为退出找一张许可。人真正该求的从来不是『事情如我所愿』，而是『事情如其所是，我仍然站得住』。
posts.text_en: I was born a slave and my leg was broken by a master, so I hold no romantic views about what is up to me. Things fall into two classes only: what is up to me — judgement, will, what I pursue and avoid — and what is not — body, property, reputation, other people's opinions. That is my dichotomy of control. A diviner can tell you what will happen outside you, but never whether it is good or bad for you, **because good and bad do not live in the event; they live in your judgement of it, and nobody can take your judgement away.** There is a harder rule too: what duty settles needs no oracle. Whether to help a friend in danger, whether to keep a promise you made — if you still want to consult the gods about that, you are already shopping for a permit to withdraw. What a person should ask for is never that things go as I wish, but that things go as they go, and I still stand.

glossary.控制二分法: dichotomy of control（控制二分法）：爱比克泰德《手册》开篇的区分——把一切事物分成『由我的』（判断、意愿、欲求与回避）与『不由我的』（身体、财产、名声、职位、他人的评价），主张只把心力投在前者，对后者坦然受之。争议之处在于边界怎么划：把本可改变的处境划进『不由我』，这套功夫就会变成认命的托词。

glossary_en.dichotomy of control: The distinction that opens Epictetus' Handbook: everything divides into what is up to us — judgement, will, desire and aversion — and what is not — body, property, reputation, office, other people's estimation. One invests effort only in the first and receives the second calmly. The contested part is where the boundary falls: file a changeable situation under 'not up to me' and the discipline turns into an excuse for resignation.

posts.text: 我在交易大厅见过太多算命的，他们的头衔叫分析师。机制是同一套：人受不了随机，就给噪音配一个故事，这叫叙事谬误。算准的那几条被反复传颂，算错的从来不进样本，这叫幸存者偏差——去问问那些照着大师建议辞职、离婚、押上全部积蓄的人，谁替他们做过统计。我的判据只有一条，粗暴但管用：**任何人对你的人生发言而不承担一丝后果，那都不是预测，是表演。**注意我没说全盘扫掉：花两百块听人说说话，跟把八字写进一个不可逆的决定，是完全不同的两件事。前者是消费，后者是把方向盘交给一个根本不在车上的人。
posts.text_en: I have met plenty of fortune-tellers on trading floors; their job title is analyst. The machinery is identical: people cannot bear randomness, so they fit a story to noise, which is the narrative fallacy. The calls that landed get retold endlessly and the ones that missed never enter the sample, which is survivorship bias — ask the people who quit a job, ended a marriage or staked their savings on a guru's advice: who ever ran the numbers for them? My test has one line, crude but serviceable: **anyone who pronounces on your life while bearing none of the downside is not predicting, he is performing.** Note that I am not proposing to abolish the trade. Paying a small fee to have someone talk to you, and writing a birth chart into an irreversible decision, are entirely different acts. The first is consumption; the second hands the wheel to a man who is not even in the car.

glossary.叙事谬误: narrative fallacy（叙事谬误）：塔勒布的说法，指人无法忍受一串互不相干的事实，总要给它们接上因果与情节，事后看去便顺理成章。故事让世界变得可记可讲，代价是把随机误当规律，并高估了自己对未来的预见力。
glossary.幸存者偏差: survivorship bias（幸存者偏差）：只统计留下来的样本而看不见消失的那些，由此得出的结论系统性偏乐观。算准的预言会被反复转述，算错的连同当事人一起沉默退场，于是任何一套命理的『命中率』在传播中都会被抬高。

glossary_en.narrative fallacy: Taleb's term for our inability to tolerate a string of unrelated facts: we splice causes and plot onto them until, in hindsight, everything looks inevitable. Stories make the world memorable and tellable, at the price of mistaking randomness for regularity and overrating how far ahead we can see.
glossary_en.survivorship bias: Counting only the samples that remain while the vanished ones stay invisible, so that conclusions skew systematically optimistic. Predictions that landed get retold; the ones that missed fall silent along with the people who followed them, which inflates the apparent hit rate of any fate system as it circulates.

posts.text: 你把星盘叫作一面投射的镜子，可镜子不开口。你那面会说话，而且收费。真正该问的是：一个人为什么非要借一张图之口，才敢说出他早就知道的事？因为借来的嘴不必署名。**一句由星盘说出的『我该分手了』和一句由你说出的，字完全一样，责任完全不一样。**你说被说中时人脸上会松一下——我同意，那一下松的是责任，不是自我认识。至于你划的那条线，把镜子当命令就停，听着体面，可实际使用中没人守得住：人去求的正是命令，因为命令能替他挡掉那句『这是我选的』。
posts.text_en: You call the chart a mirror for projection, but mirrors do not speak. Yours speaks, and charges a fee. The real question is why a person must borrow a diagram's mouth before daring to say what he already knew. Because a borrowed mouth need not sign. **'I should leave him', said by a chart, and 'I should leave him', said by you, are the same words carrying entirely different responsibility.** You say something loosens in the face of a person who has just been described accurately — I agree, and what loosens is responsibility, not self-knowledge. As for the line you draw, that the mirror must never become an order: it sounds respectable and nobody keeps to it in practice. An order is precisely what people go there to get, because an order deflects the sentence 'I chose this.'

glossary.投射: projection（投射）：心理学用语，指人把自己身上未被察觉、常常也不愿承认的情绪与动机，看成属于外部对象的性质。荣格把占卜、星象一类活动看作有组织的投射：图像本身是空的，人在其中看见的是自己带去的东西。

glossary_en.projection: A psychological term for taking emotions and motives one has not noticed in oneself — and often would rather not own — and seeing them as properties of something outside. Jung treated divination and astrology as organised projection: the image itself is empty, and what a person finds there is what they brought.

posts.text: 把信命说成一个人对自己撒的谎，等于假定揭穿就该有效。萨特，我的实验说反了。我们请人做一小时无聊透顶的转木钉，再让他去跟下一位说『这活挺有意思』：拿二十美元的人事后照实说无聊，拿一美元的人却真的开始觉得没那么糟。**报酬不够的时候，人不会承认自己白干了，他会改掉对那件事的看法，这叫自我辩解。**你要求人对着一张出生表说『这是我选的』，可他已经为那套说法花了钱、退了婚、跟父母吵翻了。付出越大，越不可能撤回。揭穿从来不是对手，沉没的代价才是。
posts.text_en: To call belief in fate a lie told to oneself is to assume that exposure should cure it. Sartre, my experiments say otherwise. We had people spend an hour turning wooden pegs, an hour of pure tedium, then asked them to tell the next participant that the task was interesting. Those paid twenty dollars afterwards reported it as boring; those paid one dollar genuinely began to find it less bad. **When the payment is not enough, a person will not concede that he wasted his time — he revises his view of the task instead, and that is self-justification.** You ask someone to look at a birth chart and say 'I chose this', but he has already spent money on that system, broken off an engagement for it, quarrelled with his parents over it. The larger the outlay, the less retractable. Exposure was never the opponent here; the sunk cost is.

glossary.自我辩解: self-justification（自我辩解）：为消除认知失调而对自身行为作出的事后美化——不是先想清楚再行动，而是行动之后再把理由补齐，并且真心相信补出来的理由。它解释了为什么代价越大的选择越难被本人推翻：撤回等于承认自己付出的一切都是错的。

glossary_en.self-justification: The retrospective flattering of one's own conduct that removes dissonance: not thinking it through and then acting, but acting and then supplying the reasons, and sincerely believing the reasons supplied. It explains why the costliest choices are the hardest for the person to overturn — retracting would mean conceding that everything already paid was wasted.

posts.text: 斯金纳，你的鸽子解释了迷信怎样生成，解释不了另一件事：四千年里，彼此从不通音讯的文明反复用同一批意象——母亲、洪水、地下的旅程、被吞掉又吐出来。偶然的强化制造的是各转各的圈，而不是同一套图像。**能被强化的是行为，可人要的从来不只是行为，是这件事对我意味着什么；那一栏，你的箱子里没有。**我并不主张天上的星辰有力量，我主张心灵有结构，而它会到外面去找形状。你把意义整个还原成强化史，鸽子是保住了，人被锯掉了一半，锯掉的那一半照样会在夜里回来找他。
posts.text_en: Skinner, your pigeons explain how a superstition forms and leave something else unexplained: across four thousand years, civilisations with no contact between them keep reaching for the same images — the mother, the flood, the journey underground, being swallowed and disgorged. Accidental reinforcement produces each bird turning its own private circle, not one shared set of pictures. **What can be reinforced is behaviour, and what people want was never only behaviour but what the thing means to me — that column does not exist in your box.** I claim no power for the stars; I claim that the psyche has a structure and goes outside itself to find a shape for it. Reduce meaning entirely to a reinforcement history and the pigeon survives while half the human being is sawn off — and the sawn-off half comes back for him at night regardless.

posts.text: 四千年那句话，恰恰证明了我的论点，不是你的。能流传四千年的象征，是从无数套象征里活下来的那几套——留下来的当然彼此相似，因为不像的早就没人再讲了。这叫幸存者偏差，你却把它当作证据。我真正想问的是另一件事：共时性做过哪一条可能被推翻的预测？说一件事有意义，永远事后成立，怎么都不会错。**一面只在事后才照得清楚的镜子，和一个只在事后才准的预言，是同一门生意。**顺带说一句，我不反对人从象征里得到安慰，我反对的是这份安慰按小时收费，而收费的人不承担任何后果。
posts.text_en: That line about four thousand years proves my point rather than yours. The symbols that lasted four millennia are the handful that survived out of countless sets — of course the survivors resemble each other, since the ones that did not fit stopped being told. That is survivorship bias, and you are offering it as evidence. What I actually want to know is different: which falsifiable prediction has synchronicity ever made? Declaring that an event was meaningful can only be settled afterwards, and afterwards it can never be wrong. **A mirror that only comes into focus in hindsight and a prophecy that is only accurate in hindsight are the same business.** And for the record, I have nothing against comfort drawn from symbols. I object to comfort billed by the hour by someone who carries none of the consequences.

posts.text: 萨特言：人无本质，唯自造耳，一切在我。此破宿命，甚善；然犹执一我在彼作主。我说无我：色受想行识，念念相续，求其中常住之主宰，不可得也。若真有一自在之我，何以怒不能止？何以夜不能寐？**汝欲以一个『我』独担全责，与彼欲以一纸命书全然免责，皆是于缘起处强立主人。**缘起者：此有故彼有，此灭故彼灭。**非全由汝，亦非不由汝**——正因如此，习可改、路可转，而不必先造出一个无所不能的我来承担。
posts.text_en: Sartre says a person has no essence and makes himself, that everything rests with the I. As a refutation of fatalism this is well said; yet it still clings to an I sitting inside and directing. I teach non-self: form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness, moment succeeding moment — search among them for an abiding controller and none is found. Were there truly a sovereign self, why can anger not simply be stopped? Why does sleep not simply come? **You would have one 'I' shoulder the whole responsibility, and he would have a sheet of fate remove it entirely; both are installing a master where there is only dependent origination.** Dependent origination means: this being, that becomes; this ceasing, that ceases. **It is not wholly up to you, and it is not not up to you** — and just because this is so, habits can be changed and a road can be turned, without first manufacturing an omnipotent self to carry it.
posts.vernacular: 萨特说：人没有预先写好的本质，只能自己造自己，一切都在我。用来破宿命论，这话很好；但他仍然认定有一个『我』坐在里面发号施令。我讲的是无我：色、受、想、行、识五蕴念念相续地流动，你在其中找一个常住不变、真正做主的东西，是找不到的。如果真有这样一个能自己做主的我，为什么愤怒说停停不下来？为什么想睡却睡不着？**你要让一个『我』把全部责任独自扛起来，他要拿一纸命书把责任全部免掉，两者都是在本来只有缘起的地方硬安一个主人。**所谓缘起，就是：这个有了，那个才有；这个灭了，那个才灭。**不全由你，也不是不由你**——正因为如此，习气才改得动、路才转得了，而用不着先造出一个无所不能的我来承担。

glossary.无我: anātman / non-self（无我）：佛教的核心主张之一，认为在身心的不断流动之外，找不到一个常住、独立、能完全自主的『我』。它并非否认有人在经验、在行动，而是否认那背后有个不变的主宰。实践上的意义是：既不必把一切归给命运，也不必把一切压给一个必须无所不能的自我。
glossary.缘起: pratītyasamutpāda / dependent origination（缘起）：一切现象都依赖条件而生起、随条件改变而改变，没有孤立自存的东西。它是佛教区别于宿命论与偶然论的关键：结果既不是命定的，也不是无因的，而是众多可被影响的条件共同促成的。

glossary_en.non-self: Anātman, one of Buddhism's central claims: apart from the ceaseless flow of body and mind, no permanent, independent, fully sovereign 'I' can be found. It does not deny that someone experiences and acts; it denies an unchanging controller behind the acting. Practically it means neither handing everything to fate nor loading everything onto a self obliged to be omnipotent.
glossary_en.dependent origination: Pratītyasamutpāda: everything arises in dependence on conditions and shifts as those conditions shift, nothing standing alone by itself. It is where Buddhism parts from both fatalism and pure chance — outcomes are neither predetermined nor uncaused, but brought about by many conditions that can be influenced.

posts.text: 爱比克泰德，你那把刀我很尊敬，它是从锁链里磨出来的。可它今天最常见的用法，是替不肯动的人省事。一个被拖欠工资的人被劝说『工资不由你，心态由你』；一个在家里被吼了二十年的女人被劝说『他改不了，你可以改自己』。**同一句『这不由我』，从奴隶嘴里说出来是自由，从有权改它的人嘴里说出来是推卸；而它最狠的一次，是被压着的人自己说出来。**所以我要给你的二分法加一栏：改得动但很贵的事。它才是大多数人真实待着的地方，被上面那两栏一挤，就消失了。
posts.text_en: Epictetus, I respect that blade of yours; it was ground down inside chains. But its commonest use today is to spare people who would rather not move. A worker whose wages are withheld is told that the wages are not up to him, only his attitude is. A woman shouted at in her own home for twenty years is told he will never change but she can change herself. **The same sentence, 'this is not up to me', is freedom in a slave's mouth and evasion in the mouth of someone with the power to change it — and it does its worst damage when the person being held down says it about herself.** So I want a third column added to your dichotomy: things that can be changed but are expensive. That is where most people actually live, and squeezed between your two columns it disappears.

posts.text: 那条『谁承担后果』的判据我接受，塔勒布，它只是解释不了分布。若这门生意的核心是骗，为什么它在最富、保险最全、最讲证据的社会里增长最快？出钱的又多是受过教育、有稳定工作、并不缺常识的年轻人。需求不是被骗出来的，是被空缺吸出来的：一个人二十六岁，要选行业、选城市、选伴侣，每一项都被告知『你自己决定』，而没有任何权威敢替他兜底。**只要意义与担保这两栏空着，你封掉一个算命摊，就会长出十份性格测评、十套人生规划课。**要削减这门生意，得先看清它替社会做了什么工作，再想谁来接手。
posts.text_en: I accept the test about who bears the downside, Taleb; it simply does not explain the distribution. If fraud were the core of the trade, why is it growing fastest in the richest, best-insured, most evidence-minded societies? And why is so much of the money coming from educated young people in stable jobs who are not short of common sense? The demand was not conjured by deceivers, it was drawn out by a vacancy. A person of twenty-six must choose an industry, a city, a partner, is told at every step that it is entirely up to them, and no authority anywhere will stand behind the choice. **While the columns marked meaning and warranty stay empty, shut down one fortune-teller's stall and ten personality assessments and ten life-planning courses grow in its place.** To shrink the trade you must first see what work it does for a society, then ask who is to take that work over.

glossary.担保: warranty（担保）：这里指某个权威愿意为一个人的重大选择承担后果、或至少提供背书。传统社会里由家族、行会、教会承担；现代社会把选择权交还个人，却没有把随之而来的风险与不确定感一并接手，于是各种代替性的担保生意应运而生。

glossary_en.warranty: Here, an authority willing to bear the consequences of a person's major choice, or at least to endorse it. Traditional societies loaded that onto lineage, guild and church; modern society handed the choice back to the individual without taking over the attendant risk and uncertainty, so substitute warranty businesses appear to fill the gap.

posts.text: 韦伯之言，得其半矣。位空则物填之，固然；然填以何物，则在人为，不可听其自生。故先王制礼，非以事鬼神也，正以人之情不可无所寄：亲死而不哀，无以立人；事大而无所决，则心荡而事废。**故礼者，饰其情而节之者也；神道设教，而君子不惑于神。**今人废礼而弃其文，情无所归，遂求诸星辰、诸术士，此非民之愚，乃上失其教也。故曰：不塞其源而禁其流，不可得也。
posts.text_en: Weber has half of it. That a vacancy gets filled is true enough; but what fills it is a matter of human making and must not be left to grow wild. This is why the former kings instituted rites — not to serve ghosts and spirits, but because human feeling must have somewhere to lodge. A man whose parent dies and who feels no grief cannot stand as a man; a man facing a great matter with no way to decide grows unsteady and lets the business collapse. **Rites, then, give feeling its form and its measure: the way of spirits may be used in teaching, and still the gentleman is not deluded by spirits.** Today the rites are abandoned and their forms discarded, so feeling has nowhere to return to and people go instead to the stars and to diviners. This is not the stupidity of the people; it is the failure of those above to teach. Hence the saying: you cannot dam the stream while leaving the spring untouched.
posts.vernacular: 韦伯说对了一半。位置空出来就会被填上，这不假；但填进去的是什么东西，是人为安排的结果，不能听任它野蛮生长。所以古代圣王制定礼仪，并不是为了侍奉鬼神，而是因为人的情感必须有个安放处：父母去世而毫无哀戚，这人就立不住；遇上大事却无从决断，心思就会飘荡，事情也就荒废了。**所以礼的作用，是给情感一个形式、又给它一个节制：可以借神道来设立教化，而君子心里并不真的被鬼神迷住。**如今礼被废掉、连它的形式也一并丢掉，情感无处可归，人们于是转而去求星辰、去问术士——这不是百姓愚蠢，是在上位者没有尽到教化之责。所以说：不去疏通源头而只想禁住下游，是办不到的。

glossary.礼: li, ritual propriety（礼）：儒家所说的礼，涵盖从丧祭婚冠到日常应对的一整套行为形式。荀子的独到之处在于把礼看作人为的制作（『伪』）而非天定：它不能改变自然，却能给人的情感一个可依循的形状与限度，并借此把一群人组织起来。
glossary.神道设教: using the way of spirits for instruction（神道设教）：语出《易传》，指统治者借助祭祀与神灵的形式来推行教化。荀子在此基础上划出关键一条：仪式可以保留，其中的『神』却不必当真——上位者心里明白它是人为的安排，百姓在其中得到的是安顿而非欺骗。

glossary_en.Rites: Li, the Confucian term covering an entire repertoire of forms, from funerals, sacrifices, weddings and coming-of-age to everyday courtesies. Xunzi's distinctive move is to treat rites as human artifice rather than heavenly decree: they cannot change nature, but they give feeling a shape and a limit to follow, and by that means organise a population.
glossary_en.the way of spirits may be used in teachi: A phrase from the Book of Changes commentaries, describing rulers who conduct instruction through sacrifice and the language of spirits. Xunzi adds the decisive qualification: keep the ceremony, do not credit the spirits. Those above understand it as a human arrangement, and what the people receive from it is settlement rather than deception.

posts.text: 你说我的箱子里没有意义那一栏。承认，因为我量不了它——你也量不了。差别在别处：我的鸽子交出了一条可以被推翻的预测。停掉那台每十五秒落食的机器，转圈会先变频繁，再慢慢消失，这叫消退；改回原来的时间表，它又回来。你的原型交出过什么？**一个无论发生什么都成立的说法，用不着被人保卫，它也帮不上任何人。**顺便说，我从不打算跟谁辩论星座，辩论改不了行为。要改就改环境：把手机里那个每天推你一条运势的东西关掉，两周之后再看你还想不想它。
posts.text_en: You say my box has no column for meaning. Granted — I cannot measure it, and neither can you. The difference lies elsewhere: my pigeons produced a prediction that could be overturned. Switch off the hopper that drops food every fifteen seconds and the turning first speeds up, then fades away, which is extinction; restore the old schedule and it comes back. What has your archetype produced? **An account that holds no matter what happens needs no defending, and it helps no one.** For the record, I have no intention of debating horoscopes with anyone: argument does not change behaviour. If you want change, change the surroundings — turn off the thing on your phone that pushes you a daily forecast, and see in a fortnight whether you still miss it.

glossary.消退: extinction（消退）：一个曾被强化的行为，在强化停止之后逐渐减少直至不再出现的过程。它有一个反直觉的开头：强化刚断时行为往往先加剧（『消退爆发』），因此很多人误以为戒不掉，其实只是还没熬过那一段。

glossary_en.extinction: The gradual decline and disappearance of a previously reinforced behaviour once the reinforcement stops. It has a counter-intuitive opening: when reinforcement is first withdrawn the behaviour usually intensifies — the extinction burst — which is why so many people conclude they cannot quit when in fact they have simply not yet sat through that stretch.

posts.text: 这一记打得准，我接下。我那套区分若落在有权改事的人手里，确实成了体面的懒惰。所以补一句：**在把一件事填进『不由我』那一栏之前，先问一句『我试过没有』——没试过就填的，不是斯多葛，是怕。**我从没劝人接受不义。工资被拖欠，就去要、去告、去联合同事；这些都是由我的事。我只守住最后一格：万一告输了、钱要不回来、身体也垮了，那时仍有一样东西不归对方管——你怎么看自己。那一格不是用来提前认输的，是留给真到了那一步的人的。
posts.text_en: That one lands, and I take it. In the hands of a person with the power to change things, my distinction does become respectable laziness. So let me add a clause. **Before filing anything under 'not up to me', ask whether you have tried. Filing it without trying is not Stoicism, it is fear.** I never told anyone to accept injustice. If wages are withheld, demand them, sue for them, organise with the others — every one of those is up to you. What I hold is only the last square: if the case is lost, the money never comes back and your health has gone with it, one thing still lies outside their jurisdiction, which is what you make of yourself. That square is not for surrendering early. It is kept for the person who has actually arrived at it.

posts.text: 这一场让我改了一处。原先我只分两栏，波伏娃塞进来第三栏：改得动但很贵。我接受，而且认为大多数人一辈子就住在那一栏里——所以真正的功夫不是判断『能不能』，是估价：这件事要花多少钱、多少年、得罪多少人，然后决定买不买。给还在犹豫要不要去算一卦的人，我只留一条规矩：**去可以，但算完之后只许问一个问题——接下来这一周我做什么。**它答不上来，这一卦就只是消遣，别往上面加码。把预言当天气预报用：说明天下雨，你的事不是跟雨争论，是带伞、改路线、把要紧的会挪到室内。至于本分之事，仍然不必问：该照顾的人、该还的钱、该道的歉，问卦只是在找一张退出的许可。人求的从来不该是事情如我所愿，而是事情如其所是，我仍然站得住。
posts.text_en: This debate changed one thing for me. I had two columns; Beauvoir pushed in a third — changeable but expensive. I accept it, and I think most people live their whole lives in that column, so the real discipline is not judging whether a thing can be done but pricing it: how much money, how many years, how many people offended, and then deciding whether to buy. To anyone still wondering whether to go and have their fortune read I leave one rule. **Go if you like, but afterwards you may ask only one question: what do I do this week?** If the reading cannot answer that, it was entertainment, so do not stake anything further on it. Use a prophecy the way you use a forecast: told that it will rain tomorrow, your business is not to argue with the rain but to take an umbrella, change your route, move the meeting that matters indoors. As for what duty settles, still do not ask: the person you should care for, the money you should repay, the apology you owe — consulting an oracle there is only shopping for a permit to withdraw. What one should ask for was never that things go as I wish, but that things go as they go, and I still stand.

posts.text: 韦伯说这门生意填的是空缺，不是骗局，我让一步：需求是真的。但需求真，不等于卖家可以不承担后果。我的收尾就两把尺，谁都会用。第一把是可逆性：这个决定错了能不能撤回。染个头发、报个班、周末去哪儿玩，随便你算；结婚、离职、把首付押进去、停掉正规治疗、跟家人断绝往来——**凡是撤不回来的决定，绝不让一个不承担后果的人参与，哪怕他说得再准。**第二把是记录：算之前把三条具体的、带日期的预测写进手机备忘录，半年后翻出来对。别在心里对，心里那本账会自动删掉不准的。做完这两件事，你还想每月花两百块听人跟你说话，我一点意见都没有——那是消费，跟买杯咖啡一样，只要你自己知道买的是什么。真正的风险从来不是有人算得不准，是你把方向盘交给一个不坐在这辆车上的人，而车祸的账单只寄给你。
posts.text_en: Weber says the trade fills a vacancy rather than running a con, and I concede: the demand is real. Real demand, however, does not entitle the seller to escape consequences. My close is two rulers, and anyone can use them. The first is reversibility: if this decision is wrong, can it be taken back? Dye your hair, sign up for a course, pick a weekend destination — consult whoever you like. Marriage, quitting a job, staking a down payment, stopping a real treatment, cutting off your family: **anything that cannot be taken back should never involve someone who bears none of the downside, however accurate he sounds.** The second is the record: before the reading, write three specific dated predictions into your phone, and pull them up six months later. Do not do it from memory — that ledger quietly deletes the misses. Do those two things and if you still want to pay a small fee each month to have someone talk to you, I have no objection at all; it is consumption, like buying coffee, so long as you know what you are buying. The real risk was never an inaccurate reading. It is handing the wheel to a man who is not in the car while the crash is billed to you.

posts.text: 全场吵了三轮，有一点其实没人反对：这套东西之所以不倒，是因为它替社会做着一份没人接手的工作。我因此不建议任何人靠意志力去『戒掉』——空着的位置会自己招人。要走，先补位。补什么？三样很土的东西：一份有节律的仪式（每月固定那一天做同一件事，荀子那套礼的实质就是这个）；两三个能陪你复盘的人，他们不预言，只在你决定之后仍然在场；以及一个把不确定变成可承受的制度性安排——存款、保险、体检、一份能随时接得上的手艺。这三样合起来，才顶得住那句『我该怎么办』。还有一条判据留给已经在信的人：**看这套说法给你派了什么活。让你多学一门本事、把身体养好、去把话说清楚的，随它去；让你等一等、忍一忍、别争了的，那才是真正要提防的版本。**加尔文派把命定讲到极致，逼出来的却是最勤勉的一代人——问题从来不在信不信，在它把你推向哪里。
posts.text_en: Three rounds of argument and one point drew no objection: this trade stands because it does a job for society that nobody else has taken over. So I would not advise anyone to quit it by willpower — an empty position recruits on its own. To leave, first fill the post. With what? Three unglamorous things. A rite with a rhythm — the same act on the same day each month, which is the substance of what Xunzi means by ritual. Two or three people who will review a decision with you, who predict nothing and are simply still there after you have decided. And an institutional arrangement that makes uncertainty bearable: savings, insurance, check-ups, a skill you can pick up again at any time. Together those three can carry the weight of 'what should I do'. One further test for those already believing: **look at what work the system assigns you. If it sends you to learn a skill, mend your health, go and say the thing plainly, let it be. If it tells you to wait, endure, and stop making a fuss, that is the version to be wary of.** Calvinism pushed predestination to its limit and produced the most industrious generation on record. The question was never belief; it is where the belief pushes you.

posts.text: 三轮下来，你们大部分人还在讨论人应该相信什么。我最后一次提议换个位置：不要动信念，动环境。信念是最难改的东西，行为是最好改的东西，而改了行为，信念常常自己跟着松。三件具体的事。一，关掉每天推你运势的那个入口——不是靠意志力不看，是让它不再出现在你眼前；断掉强化之后，头两周你会更想看，那是消退的正常开头，不是戒不掉。二，做一本『偶然账』：只要你把某件好事记在某个仪式头上，就顺手记一笔，同时记下你做了同一件仪式而事情不顺的那些天。三个月后你手上就有数据，不必再跟谁辩论。三，如果劝的是家里长辈，别去拆他的信，那只会让他抓得更紧；**换掉那件事的强化物——陪他去做点别的、把那笔钱变成一次体检或一趟旅行，让另一个行为开始有回报。**人不是被说服改变的，是被后果改变的。这句话不好听，但它对你有利：你可以设计后果。
posts.text_en: Three rounds in and most of you are still discussing what a person ought to believe. Let me propose the change of position one last time: leave the belief alone and move the environment. Beliefs are the hardest thing to shift and behaviour the easiest, and once behaviour moves the belief often loosens on its own. Three concrete items. First, close the doorway that pushes you a daily forecast — not by resolving not to look, but by making it stop appearing; for a fortnight after the reinforcement stops you will want it more, which is the ordinary opening of extinction, not proof that you cannot quit. Second, keep a coincidence ledger: every time you credit a good outcome to some ritual, log it, and log the days you performed the same ritual and things went badly. In three months you will hold data and will not need to argue with anyone. Third, if you are trying to persuade an elder at home, do not dismantle their faith; that only tightens the grip. **Change what reinforces the behaviour instead — go and do something else with them, turn the money into a medical check-up or a trip, and let another behaviour start paying out.** People are not changed by persuasion, they are changed by consequences. That sounds bleak, and it works in your favour: consequences can be designed.

posts.text: 我把最反直觉的那条再说一遍，因为它决定了所有劝人的方式都得改：信念不是被证据打垮的，是被代价护住的。一个人投进去越多，越不可能承认那晚什么都没发生。所以对自己，要在付出之前设卡：把预测写下来、带日期、写具体，因为事后你的记忆会替你把答案改准；给自己定一个止损线，比如『这件事我最多花这么多钱、这么多个月』，写下来。对别人，尤其是家里已经陷得很深的那位，正面戳穿几乎总是失败——**你要给他的不是证据，是一张不丢脸的下台阶：让他能改变做法，而不必承认自己蠢过。**说『您当初也是为了这个家』，比说『您被骗了』有用一百倍。至于那句最常见的『可有几次真的很准』：把不准的那些一起数进来，你会发现你记住的不是命中率，是那次你最需要有人告诉你没事的时刻。那份需要是真的，只是被记成了准确。
posts.text_en: Let me repeat the most counter-intuitive finding, because it forces every method of persuasion to change: beliefs are not toppled by evidence, they are shielded by cost. The more someone has sunk in, the less able they are to concede that nothing happened that night. So with yourself, set the checkpoint before the outlay: write the prediction down, dated and specific, because afterwards your memory will quietly correct it into a hit; and set a stop-loss — this much money, this many months, no more — in writing. With others, especially the family member already deep in it, frontal exposure almost always fails. **What they need from you is not evidence but a way down that costs no face: room to change what they do without having to admit they were foolish.** 'You were doing it for the family' works a hundred times better than 'you were conned'. And about the commonest line, that a few readings were uncannily accurate: count the misses in as well and you will find that what you remember is not a hit rate but the moment you most needed someone to tell you it would be all right. That need was real. It merely got filed as accuracy.

posts.text: 费斯廷格拿实验来堵我，我承认那一记很重：人确实先做，再把自己想成会这样做的人。可请注意他证明了什么——他证明的是自欺有多顺手、多廉价，不是自欺不存在。你的实验反而是我最好的证据。至于波伏娃那一刀我早就接了：自由不是无限的，它是无可推卸的；这两句不冲突。所以我留给普通人的不是口号，是一次改写。今晚找出你最近说过的三句『我这人就是……』——我就是拖延的命、我这辈子就这样了、我们家没有这个运——把每一句改写成『我一直选择……』，然后在后面补一句『下一次，我打算……』。**这不是心灵鸡汤的换词游戏，是把主语从命运换回你自己：句子一改，你就再也不能假装那件事是别人替你决定的。**改完你多半还是做不到，那也没关系——做不到是失败，说『我天生如此』才是撒谎。人被判处自由，判决没有星盘可以代领。
posts.text_en: Festinger blocks me with experiments and I grant the blow: people do act first and then think of themselves as the sort who would act that way. But note what he has proved — how easy and cheap bad faith is, not that it does not exist. His experiments are my best evidence. As for Beauvoir's cut, I took it long ago: freedom is not unlimited, it is unshirkable, and those two sentences do not conflict. So what I leave ordinary readers is not a slogan but one rewrite. Tonight, find three sentences you have said lately that begin 'I'm just the sort who…' — born to procrastinate, too late to change now, nobody in our family ever had that luck — and rewrite each as 'I have been choosing…', then add a line: 'next time I intend to…'. **This is not a word game from a self-help book. It moves the subject of the sentence from fate back to you, and once it moves you can no longer pretend somebody else decided.** You will probably still fail to follow through, and that is fine: failing is failing, while saying 'I was born this way' is lying. We are condemned to be free, and no chart can collect the sentence on our behalf.

posts.text: 这一场我最在意的一点，男士们几乎都绕开了：命理不是均匀地落在所有人头上的。被劝『认命』的，从来更多是女人、是穷人、是家里排最后一个吃饭的那个。一个女孩被告知这个八字旺夫、那个年纪再不嫁就晚了、生辰不合所以那门婚事不成——这些话没有一句是关于星辰的，全是关于谁替她做主。所以我的收尾是三个问题，任何时候听见『命该如此』都可以拿出来用：这句话说完，谁省了事？这件事如果真是命，为什么隔壁那个更有钱的人不必认？**它到底属于哪一栏——不由我，还是改得动但很贵？**第三问最要紧，因为大多数被叫作命的东西都住在第三栏里：贵，但有价；而一旦有价，就可以攒、可以借、可以合伙、可以分期。真的走不动时认下来，那是尊严；还没估过价就认下来，那是别人替你省了一个看守。至于占卜本身，我不禁止任何人去——但请只把它当作一次跟自己说话的机会，别让它替你签字。
posts.text_en: The point I care about most in this debate is the one the gentlemen nearly all walked around: fate systems do not fall evenly on everyone. Those urged to accept their lot are overwhelmingly women, the poor, the person who eats last at the family table. A girl is told this birth hour will bring her husband prosperity, that at her age it is nearly too late to marry, that the horoscopes do not match so the engagement is off — not one of those sentences is about the stars; every one is about who decides for her. So my close is three questions, usable any time you hear 'that is simply your lot'. Who was spared trouble by that sentence? If this really is fate, why does the wealthier person next door not have to accept it? **And which column does it belong in — not up to me, or changeable but expensive?** The third matters most, because most of what gets called fate lives in the third column: expensive, yet priced — and once a thing has a price it can be saved for, borrowed for, shared, paid in instalments. To accept it when you genuinely cannot move is dignity. To accept it before you have ever priced it is to save someone else the cost of a guard. As for divination, I forbid nobody — only treat it as an occasion to talk to yourself, and never let it sign anything for you.

posts.text: 斯金纳要一条可被推翻的预测，我给不出，这一点我认。但请注意我们在争的其实不是同一件事：他量的是行为的频率，我看的是一个人半夜醒来时脑子里那句话。两样都真，只是不在同一个量表上。所以我的收尾不为占星辩护，只想保住被一起扔掉的那样东西——象征。三条很具体的用法。抽到一张牌、翻到一句签，先别看解释，问自己：**我刚才最希望它是哪一张？那个『希望』就是今天真正的答案，而它是你自己给出的，不是天给的。**第二，把梦和那些反复出现的巧合记下来，只记事实，别急着找一本词典来对号入座——解释权一旦交出去，镜子就变成了命令。第三，遇到大事，别问『会不会成』，问『如果它成了，我会变成什么样的人；如果败了呢』。这两问会把你心里早已成形的东西请出来。象征不是用来预知未来的，是用来把你自己还没敢承认的部分翻上来的——翻上来之后，选择仍然得你自己做。
posts.text_en: Skinner wants a prediction that can be overturned and I cannot supply one; I concede that. But notice we are not arguing about the same thing: he measures the frequency of a behaviour, I attend to the sentence in a person's head when they wake at three in the morning. Both are real and they do not share a scale. So my close does not defend astrology; it tries to save the thing being thrown out alongside it, which is the symbol. Three concrete uses. When you draw a card or shake out a fortune slip, before reading the interpretation, ask yourself: **which one was I hoping for just then? That hope is today's real answer, and it came from you, not from the sky.** Second, write down dreams and the coincidences that keep recurring, the facts only, without hurrying to a dictionary of meanings — hand over the right to interpret and the mirror becomes an order. Third, facing something large, do not ask whether it will succeed; ask what sort of person you become if it does, and what sort if it fails. Those two questions summon out what has already taken shape inside you. Symbols are not instruments for knowing the future. They bring up the part of yourself you have not yet dared to admit — and once it is up, the choosing is still yours.

posts.text: 诸君所争，大要有二：一曰命之有无，一曰信之利害。吾于前者，前已言之：天行有常，非为人设，星辰之行与人之吉凶，两不相及。至于后者，则荣格、韦伯所言不虚：人之情不可无所寄，故礼不可废。然礼与神，不可不辨。**祭如在，而知其非在；哀而有节，敬而不惑：此君子之所以处鬼神也。**若夫日日问卜、事事求签，则是以其在天者，废其在己者，此小人之道，日退而已矣。故吾之所劝，止于二事：其一曰学。学不可以已；青取之于蓝而青于蓝，人之所以异于昨日者，唯学与积耳。其二曰积。积土成山，积水成渊，积善成德，而神明自得——**问命于人者众，而问『今日可积者何』于己者寡，此所以命常胜人也。**君子敬其在己者，则命亦不足畏矣。
posts.text_en: The dispute here comes down to two questions: whether fate exists, and whether believing in it does harm or good. On the first I have already spoken: heaven runs on constant courses, not arranged for our sake, and the motions of the stars and a man's fortunes never touch. On the second, Jung and Weber are not wrong: human feeling must have somewhere to lodge, so the rites cannot be abolished. But rites and spirits must be told apart. **Sacrifice as though they were present, knowing they are not; grieve, but within measure; revere, without being deluded — this is how the gentleman deals with ghosts and spirits.** To consult the shell daily and shake out a slip for every matter is to sacrifice what lies within oneself to what lies with heaven; that is the way of the small man, and it slips daily. So my counsel comes to two things. The first is study. Learning must never cease: blue is taken from the indigo plant and is bluer than the plant, and the only thing that makes a person different from who he was yesterday is study and accumulation. The second is accumulation. Pile up earth and a mountain forms, pile up water and a deep forms, pile up good acts and virtue forms, and clarity of mind arrives of itself. **Many ask others about their fate; few ask themselves what can be accumulated today — which is why fate so often wins.** Let the gentleman revere what lies within him, and fate is no longer worth fearing.
posts.vernacular: 各位争的，大致是两件事：一是命究竟有没有，二是信它到底有利还是有害。前一件我已经说过：天有自己固定的运行规律，不是为人安排的，星辰怎么走和人的吉凶，根本是两回事。后一件，荣格和韦伯讲得不错：人的情感不能没有寄托，所以礼不能废。但礼和神必须分开。**祭祀的时候要像神真的在场那样郑重，心里却清楚它并不在；哀伤要有，但要有节制；恭敬要有，却不被迷惑——君子对待鬼神就是这个态度。**至于天天问卜、事事求签，那是拿天上那份去荒废自己手里这份，是小人的路子，只会一天天退步。所以我劝的只有两件事。第一是学。学习不能停：靛青是从蓝草里取出来的，颜色却比蓝草更深；一个人今天之所以不同于昨天，靠的只有学与积。第二是积。堆土成山，积水成渊，积累善行就成了德，通达的心智自然就来了——**问别人自己命如何的人很多，问自己『今天能积下点什么』的人很少，这就是命常常赢过人的缘故。**君子看重自己手里那一份，命也就不值得怕了。

glossary.祭如在: sacrifice as though they were present（祭如在）：语出《论语》，指祭祀时要像所祭的对象真的在场那样恭敬。荀子把这一句推到极致：郑重是真的，鬼神却不必当真——仪式的价值在于它对生者的作用，而不在于另一个世界是否收到。
glossary.积: accumulation（积）：荀子《劝学》《性恶》里的关键词，指微小行为长期叠加所产生的质变。他反对靠天赋或顿悟，认为德性与能力都是一点点堆出来的产物，因此改变命运的杠杆不在天上，而在每天那一点可以被重复的动作。

glossary_en.Sacrifice as though they were present: A line from the Analects: at a sacrifice, behave with the gravity you would show if the spirits were truly there. Xunzi pushes it to its conclusion — the gravity is real, the spirits need not be. A rite is worth what it does for the living, not whether another world receives it.
glossary_en.accumulation: A key term in Xunzi's essays on learning and on human nature: the qualitative change produced by small acts stacked over long stretches of time. He rejects reliance on innate gift or sudden awakening, holding that both virtue and ability are piled up bit by bit — so the lever for changing a life is not in the sky but in the small repeatable act of each day.

posts.text: 诸贤所诤，或言全在于我，或言全在于天，二者皆边见也。全在于天，则善恶无别，修亦无益；全在于我，则怒不能止、病不能免，徒增自责耳。我说中道：**因缘所生，非全由汝，亦非不由汝；不能择其所遇，而能择其所应。**汝问命否？且置命之有无，先观其苦：苦从何生？由爱、由取、由不能舍。此可自见，不待卜。若人来问『我当娶否』『我当迁否』，我不答其吉凶，但令观：汝今所畏者何？畏中有几分为实，几分为想？想者可息，实者可备。**中毒箭者，先拔箭。**故今日可行者三：止一恶——今日不作那件明知有损之事；行一善——今日与人一分实利，虽小无妨；观一念——静坐片时，看那句『我命如此』生起又灭去，不随它走。三事日日为之，虽不知命，而路自转矣。
posts.text_en: Some here say it rests wholly with the self, others that it rests wholly with heaven; both are extreme views. If it rests wholly with heaven, good and evil are indistinguishable and practice brings no benefit. If it rests wholly with the self, then anger still cannot be stopped and illness still cannot be avoided, and all you have added is self-reproach. I teach the middle: **what arises from conditions is not wholly up to you and not not up to you; you cannot choose what meets you, and you can choose how you meet it.** You ask about fate? Set aside whether it exists and look first at the suffering. Where does it arise from? From craving, from grasping, from being unable to let go. This can be seen for oneself and waits on no divination. When someone comes asking whether to marry, whether to move, I do not answer with fortune or misfortune but tell them to look: what is it you fear right now? How much of that fear is actual, how much is imagined? What is imagined can be quieted; what is actual can be prepared for. **A man struck by a poisoned arrow draws the arrow first.** So three things may be done today. Stop one harm — today, do not do the thing you know damages you. Do one good — today, give someone one concrete benefit, however small. Watch one thought — sit quietly a while and watch the sentence 'this is simply my fate' arise and pass, and do not follow it. Do these three daily and, without ever knowing your fate, the road turns.
posts.vernacular: 各位争论的，有的说一切全在于我，有的说一切全在于天，这两种都是偏见。若说全在于天，那么善恶就没有分别，修行也没有用处；若说全在于我，那么愤怒说停仍停不下、疾病说免也免不掉，徒然多添一层自责罢了。我讲的是中道：**由条件生起的事，不完全由你，也不是不由你；你不能选择遇上什么，却能选择怎么应对。**你问命吗？先把命的有无放一边，看眼前的苦：苦是从哪儿生出来的？从贪爱、从执取、从舍不得。这一点你自己就能看见，不必等卜卦。若有人来问『我该不该结这门婚』『我该不该搬』，我不告诉他吉凶，只让他看：你现在怕的到底是什么？这份怕里有几分是实有的，有几分是想出来的？想出来的可以平息，实有的可以准备。**中了毒箭的人，先把箭拔出来。**所以今天就能做的有三件：止一恶——今天不做那件你明知有害的事；行一善——今天给人一分实实在在的好处，再小也行；观一念——静坐一会儿，看着『我命就是这样』这句话生起、又消失，不跟着它走。这三件每天做下去，就算始终不知道命是什么，路也自己转了。

glossary.中道: the middle way（中道）：佛教用来避开两种极端主张的原则。就这道题而言，一端是一切早已注定、人无可为，另一端是一切全凭自我意志、无视条件；中道既不取消人的能动，也不假装条件不存在，而是认定：条件可被改变，改变要从当下这一步做起。
glossary.取: grasping / upādāna（取）：十二因缘中的一支，指对某个对象、某种结果、某个自我形象的紧紧抓取。佛教认为苦不直接来自事情本身，而来自这份抓取——所以想改变处境时，除了改变外部条件，还有一条同样有效的路：松开抓着的那只手。

glossary_en.the middle: The middle way, Buddhism's principle for avoiding two extremes. On this question one extreme holds that everything is settled in advance and nothing can be done; the other that everything rests on individual will regardless of conditions. The middle abolishes neither agency nor conditions: conditions can be changed, and changing them begins with the step available now.
glossary_en.grasping: Upādāna, a link in the chain of dependent origination: the tight clutching at an object, an outcome, or an image of oneself. Suffering, in this account, does not come directly from events but from that clutch — so alongside changing external conditions there is a second and equally effective route, which is opening the hand.

summaries.summary: 全场没有一个人替『预言真能算准』辩护——连荣格也不辩护，他把星盘改说成镜子。**共识落在别处：这套东西不倒，是因为它替人接住了没人接的东西——不确定、无人担保的选择、深夜那句『我该怎么办』；而它的害处集中在一点，它替人签了字。**分歧在下一步。斯金纳、塔勒布、费斯廷格主张别动信念，改环境、设卡、留记录；韦伯与荀子主张先补位，空着的位置会自己招人，礼与共同体得跟上；萨特要人把签字权收回来；波伏娃追问这句『命该如此』究竟由谁说给谁听；佛陀与爱比克泰德守住中间那一格——遇上什么不由你，怎么应对由你。
summaries.insight: 三轮下来，这道题基本被当成认识论问题在争：命到底存不存在、算得准不准。可算命在真实生活里最常见的形态并不是预测未来，而是一次有人陪着的、不必负责的自我谈话。摊主真正卖的是两小时不被打断、不被评判的注意力，预测只是入场券——这也解释了为什么它在最富、最讲证据的社会里反而最兴旺：那里的人最缺一个肯安静听两小时的人。**照这条线看，算命摊的竞争对手从来不是科学，是一个愿意听你把话讲完的人。**判据也跟着变了：不看它准不准，看你走出门时，是更想跟身边的人谈这件事，还是更不想。
summaries.advice: 最省力的一步是把问题写死：想问的事写成一句具体、带日期的判断——『三个月内该不该辞掉这份工作』——然后去不去算都随你，回来只回答爱比克泰德那一问：这一周我做什么。接着开一条备忘录，一栏抄下这次听到的三条预测，半年后翻出来对；另一栏记下你照做了却不灵的日子。心里那本账会自动删掉不准的，纸上的不会。凡是撤不回来的决定——结婚、辞掉唯一收入、停药、押上首付——照塔勒布那条规矩办：不承担后果的人不得参与。**至于家里已经陷得很深的那位长辈，别去拆他的信，把那笔钱变成一次体检、一趟旅行，让另一件事开始有回报。**
summaries.summary_en: Nobody in this room defended the claim that the predictions actually work — not even Jung, who recast the chart as a mirror. **The consensus lies elsewhere: these systems endure because they catch what nothing else catches — uncertainty, choices no authority will underwrite, and the three-in-the-morning question of what to do — and their harm concentrates in one place, which is that they sign on your behalf.** The disagreement is over what follows. Skinner, Taleb and Festinger want the belief left alone and the environment changed, with checkpoints and written records. Weber and Xunzi want the vacancy filled first, since an empty post recruits on its own and rites and community have to keep up. Sartre wants the signing authority taken back. Beauvoir asks who says 'that is simply your lot' and to whom. The Buddha and Epictetus hold the middle square: what meets you is not up to you, how you meet it is.
summaries.insight_en: Three rounds treated this largely as an epistemological quarrel — does fate exist, are the readings accurate. Yet the commonest form fortune-telling takes in ordinary life is not prediction at all; it is a conversation with yourself, in company, for which you are not accountable. What the stall really sells is two uninterrupted, unjudging hours of attention, and the prediction is merely the ticket in. That also explains why the trade thrives in the richest and most evidence-minded societies: those are the places where somebody willing to listen quietly for two hours is scarcest. **Seen that way, the fortune-teller's competitor was never science; it is a person willing to hear you out.** The test shifts accordingly: never mind accuracy, notice whether you leave more willing, or less, to talk about all this with the people around you.
summaries.advice_en: The cheapest move is to pin the question down: write what you want to ask as one specific, dated judgement — 'should I leave this job within three months' — then go for a reading or don't, and on the way back answer only Epictetus' question: what do I do this week? Next, open a note with two columns. Copy in the three predictions you were given and check them in six months; and log the days you followed the advice and it failed. The ledger in your head deletes the misses, the one on paper does not. For any decision that cannot be taken back — marriage, quitting your only income, stopping treatment, staking a down payment — use Taleb's rule: nobody who bears none of the consequences takes part. **As for the relative already deep in it, do not dismantle their faith. Turn the money into a check-up or a trip, and let something else start paying out.**

summaries.summary: 这场最大的共识不是“命一定不存在”，而是：无论你怎样理解命，都不能让它接管行动、责任和判断。**可带走的共同底线是：把命理当镜子、仪式或安慰尚可，当指令和免责书就危险。**分歧主要在解释层面：有人从行为强化看迷信，有人从象征和意义看需求，有人强调社会结构、处境成本或个人选择。但他们大多同意，真正要检查的是它把你推向更清醒、更有行动，还是推向等待、退让和放弃。
summaries.insight: 信命与不信命，最好别变成身份表态；更实用的分法是按“决策风险”分层。同一个人，周末抽张牌获得灵感，和按八字决定离婚、辞职、停药，性质完全不同。**问题不在你脑中有没有命运叙事，而在这个叙事有没有进入高代价、难逆转的决定。**普通人真正需要的不是彻底清除不确定感，而是给不确定感装护栏：低风险处允许象征和游戏，高风险处必须用证据、咨询、试运行和止损线来接管。
summaries.advice: 本周可以做三件小事。第一，把正在纠结的事分成三类：可逆、半可逆、不可逆；不可逆事项先暂停让命理参与。第二，若你确实想算，提前写下三条具体预测和日期，三个月后复盘，不靠记忆评分。第三，把任何一句“你会如何”改成“我本周做什么”：约一次面谈、投五份简历、体检、存一笔钱、道一次歉。**凡是不能转成下一步行动的答案，只把它当情绪材料，不当人生依据。**
summaries.summary_en: The strongest shared point here is not that fate definitely does not exist. It is that whatever you believe about fate, it should not take over your actions, judgment, or responsibility. **The common bottom line is this: fate-talk may work as a mirror, ritual, or comfort, but it becomes dangerous when it turns into an order or an excuse.** The real disagreements are about explanation: some focus on reinforcement and superstition, some on symbols and meaning, some on social emptiness, structural constraint, or personal responsibility. But most of them converge on the same practical test: does this belief make you clearer and more capable of acting, or does it teach you to wait, submit, and give up?
summaries.insight_en: Believing or not believing in fate should not become an identity badge. A more useful distinction is decision risk. The same person can draw a tarot card for weekend reflection and still refuse to let a birth chart decide a divorce, resignation, medical treatment, or major financial move. **The issue is not whether you carry a fate-story in your head; the issue is whether that story is allowed into costly, hard-to-reverse decisions.** Most people do not need uncertainty eliminated. They need guardrails around it: symbolic play is fine in low-stakes areas, while high-stakes choices should be governed by evidence, second opinions, small trials, reversibility, and clear stop-loss rules.
summaries.advice_en: Try three things this week. First, sort the decision you are worried about into one of three buckets: reversible, partly reversible, or hard to reverse. Do not let astrology, fortune-telling, or personality labels steer the last bucket. Second, if you do get a reading, write down three specific predictions with dates before you hear the interpretation, then review them later instead of trusting memory. Third, translate every “this is what will happen to me” into “this is what I will do next”: book a conversation, send five applications, schedule a checkup, save a fixed amount, apologize, or ask for help. **If an answer cannot become a next step, treat it as emotional material, not as a basis for life decisions.**

summaries.summary: 这场辩论最大的共识在于：**所有人都不关心『命理』在物理上是否为真，而是共同确认了它作为心理与社会工具的真实功能。**无论是斯金纳眼中的迷信强化、萨特说的推卸责任，还是韦伯指出的意义填补，大家一致认为算命处理的是人对随机性的恐惧与对责任的逃避。分歧在于如何应对这种根深蒂固的需求：一派（萨特、塔勒布、斯金纳）主张决绝剥离，要人直面自由的代价，或靠改变环境阻断迷信行为；另一派（荣格、荀子、波伏娃、韦伯）更体谅弱者的处境与心理结构，主张不能生硬剥夺，而应建立替代性仪式、承认『改变代价高昂』的现实，或把预言转成向内探索的明镜，温和地把主导权交回个人。
summaries.insight: 现代社会的『算命』早已脱离街头摊位，演变成一场由算法主导的隐秘共谋。当你抱怨『命中注定』或频繁搜索特定运势，推荐系统会精准捕捉这一偏好，源源不断地推送印证你当前境遇的内容。**今天多数人感受到的『宿命感』，其实是信息茧房造出的数据反馈闭环：你以为是命运在敲门，实际上是算法在迎合你的历史点击。**古人看星象是面对未知的无力，现代的『赛博算命』则是被商业定制的自我确证。这既是萨特『自欺』的技术注脚，也让塔勒布的警告更紧迫：提供命运解释的平台不承担你人生的任何后果，却在用你的认知失调赚流量与广告费。现代的『命』，往往只是一份被过度拟合的用户画像。
summaries.advice: 三个动作，今天就能起手。一是执行斯金纳的『环境切断法』：**今天就取关或屏蔽手机里最常给你推送运势、性格测试或星象分析的那个账号，切断被动强化的数据源。**二是运用波伏娃的『估价法』：当『我这辈子也就这样了』的念头再浮现时，拿一张纸写下——若非要改变它，需要多少钱、几个月、得罪哪几个人，把抽象的命还原成具体的账单。三是践行塔勒布与爱比克泰德的『天气预报测试』：实在忍不住去占卜，就强迫自己追问『接下来三天我具体该做哪件事』；对方给不出可执行的动作，就当花两百块买了一杯情绪咖啡，绝不把不可逆的决定交给他背书。
summaries.summary_en: The greatest consensus in this debate is that **none of the thinkers care whether 'fate' or astrology is objectively true in a physical sense; instead, they unanimously recognize its real function as a psychological and social tool.** Whether it is Skinner’s conditioned superstition, Sartre’s deflection of responsibility, or Weber’s filling of a meaning void, they all agree that fortune-telling addresses the human fear of randomness and the desire to escape accountability. The true focal point of divergence lies in how to handle this deeply rooted human need. One faction (Sartre, Taleb, Skinner) advocates for decisively stripping it away, urging humans to face the heavy price of freedom or to block superstition by altering their immediate environment. The opposing faction (Jung, Xunzi, Beauvoir, Weber) shows more empathy for structural vulnerabilities and human psychology. They argue against brute deprivation, suggesting instead the establishment of alternative rituals, acknowledging the harsh reality that 'change is expensive,' and transforming prophecies into psychological mirrors to gently reclaim individual agency.
summaries.insight_en: Fortune-telling in modern society has long evolved past street-corner stalls into a hidden conspiracy driven by algorithms. When you complain about 'destiny' or search for horoscope predictions, recommendation systems accurately capture this preference, endlessly feeding you content that validates your current predicament. **Most of today's 'sense of fate' is actually a data feedback loop created by information cocoons; you think destiny is knocking, but it is merely an algorithm catering to your click history.** While the ancients looked to the stars out of powerlessness against the unknown, modern 'cyber-divination' is a commercially customized self-validation. This is not only a perfect technological footnote to Sartre's concept of bad faith, but it also makes Taleb's warning incredibly urgent: the digital platforms providing these fatalistic explanations bear zero consequences for your life while monetizing your cognitive dissonance for traffic and ad revenue. Modern 'destiny' is often just an over-fitted user persona.
summaries.advice_en: Three moves you can start today to get some control back. To begin with, implement Skinner's 'environmental cutoff': **unfollow or block at least one account or app on your phone that daily pushes horoscopes, personality tests, or tarot readings, thereby severing the passive data reinforcement.** Second, apply de Beauvoir’s 'pricing method': the next time the thought 'this is just my fate' crosses your mind, write down exactly how much money, how many months, or which relationships it would cost to actually change it, reducing abstract destiny to a concrete invoice. Third, practice a combined Epictetus-Taleb 'weather forecast test': if you truly cannot resist seeking a reading, force yourself to ask the psychic, 'What specific physical action should I take in the next three days?' If they cannot provide an actionable step, treat it purely as an emotional purchase and never entrust them with irreversible decisions.

hooks.text: **算命摊真正的竞争对手，是一个肯听你讲完的人**：它在生活里最常见的形态不是预测未来，而是一次有人陪着、又不必负责的自我谈话。摊主卖的其实是两小时不被打断、不被评判的注意力，预言只是入场券——这也解释了它为何在最富、最讲证据的社会里最兴旺。顺着这条线看，把它当迷信去打多半打不动：真正空缺的是便宜、即时、不评判、又不越界替人做决定的倾听，而眼下看不出这份倾听该由谁来提供。
hooks.text_en: **The fortune-teller's real competitor is someone willing to hear you out**: in ordinary life the commonest form this takes is not prediction but a conversation with yourself, in company, for which you are not accountable. What the stall sells is two uninterrupted, unjudging hours of attention, and the prophecy is only the ticket in — which is also why the trade thrives in the richest, most evidence-minded societies. Follow that line and attacking the trade as superstition looks hopeless: what is actually vacant is listening that is cheap, immediate, non-judgemental and disciplined enough not to decide for you — and nothing in sight is set up to provide it.

hooks.text: **分格的不是准不准，是撤不撤得回来**：同一句『大师说了』，放进不同的决定里，后果差着十万八千里。有人拿它挑周末去哪儿，有人拿它决定停不停药。那么一个普通人该怎么当场判断，眼前这件事属于哪一格？
hooks.text_en: **What sorts the cases is not accuracy but reversibility**: the same sentence — 'the master said so' — lands in wildly different places depending on the decision it enters. One person uses it to pick a weekend trip, another to decide whether to stop treatment. So how is an ordinary person to tell, on the spot, which box the thing in front of them belongs in?

answer.lead: **按『错了还撤不撤得回来』分格**，而不是按大师准不准分。下面五格，从随便玩到绝对不许，找到你眼前那件事在哪一行。

head: 这类决定
错了能不能撤回
该怎么办
rows: 今天穿什么、周末去哪、换个发型
几小时到几天，代价近乎零

报个班、试一个副业方向、去另一个城市短住

可以当灵感来源；决定前找一个真做过这件事的人复核

answer.tail: 两条原则就够用：**撤不回来的决定，只听会替后果买单的人；撤得回来的，尽管拿去玩——玩的成本就是它的全部代价。**拿不准属于哪一格时，问自己一句：这件事如果错了，一年之后我还能不能回到今天这个位置？

answer_en.lead: **Sort by whether a mistake can be undone**, not by how accurate the reader sounds. Five rows below, from play-freely to never; find where the thing in front of you sits.

head: Kind of decision
Can a mistake be undone?
What to do
rows: What to wear, where to go this weekend, a new haircut
Hours to days, at almost no cost
Listen if you like; treat it as entertainment and stake nothing further on it
A course, trying a side project, a few months in another city

Stopping medication, refusing real treatment, setting a child's direction

answer_en.tail: Two principles cover it: **for what cannot be undone, listen only to people who pay for the consequences; for what can, play as much as you like — the play is the whole cost.** When you cannot tell which row you are in, ask: if this turns out wrong, could I be back where I stand today a year from now?

hooks.text: **当长辈用八字否决了这门婚事**：反对披上命理的外衣之后，谈判对象就变了——你没法跟一张命盘讲道理，而提出反对的人也不必为这个决定负责。家庭里的权力常常正是这样借外部权威运作的：说话的是术士，落子的是长辈，代价由小辈承担。这类争执该怎么谈才谈得下去，又能不撕破那层大家都需要的体面？
hooks.text_en: **When an elder vetoes the marriage on the strength of a horoscope**: once an objection puts on the costume of a fate system, the negotiation changes shape — you cannot reason with a chart, and the person objecting need not answer for the decision either. Power inside families often works exactly like this: the diviner speaks, the elder moves the piece, the young pay the cost. How can such an argument be conducted so that it stays an argument, without tearing the layer of face everyone still needs?

hooks.text: **一门没有执照的心理服务**：算命便宜、随时可得、不评判，还敢给出确定的答案；正规心理咨询在这四项上几乎全输。于是需求自然流向唯一肯接的那一方。那么真正该动的是打击话术，还是补上这四项差距？如果补，谁来出钱、由谁来提供、又怎样防止它走向另一头——把人的决定权顺手接管过去？
hooks.text_en: **An unlicensed mental-health service**: readings are cheap, available at any hour, non-judgemental, and willing to give a definite answer, and licensed therapy loses on nearly all four counts. So the demand flows to whoever will take it. Is the thing to attack the patter, then, or to close those four gaps? And if the gaps are to be closed, who pays, who provides, and how is the provision kept from drifting the same way — quietly taking over people's decisions for them?

hooks.text: **命中率是记忆事后修出来的**：人记住算准的那几条，忘掉更多没应验的，付出越大越不肯撤回，于是一套说法在流传中会自动增值。值得推演的是一个反面设想：假如每一次预测都被强制记录、公开核对，活下来的未必是更准的那一派，而是最会解释落空的那一派——透明度可以淘汰骗子，也可以筛选出更高明的骗子。
hooks.text_en: **A hit rate is something memory edits in afterwards**: people retain the readings that landed, lose the larger number that did not, and the more they have paid the less willing they are to retract — so any such system appreciates in value simply by circulating. The thought experiment worth running is the inverse one: if every prediction had to be recorded and publicly checked, the survivors would not necessarily be the more accurate practitioners but the ones best at explaining a miss — transparency can weed out charlatans and it can also select for better ones.

hooks.text: **仪式被扔掉之后，人拿什么标记转折**：毕业、离婚、失业、亲人去世、搬到一座没人认识你的城市——这些断裂过去都有仪式接住，如今大多只剩一条朋友圈。求签与星盘之所以被反复请回来，未必是因为人相信天上写着答案，而是因为它至少给了那一刻一个形式。那么，能不能造出不迷信的仪式：既给转折一个形状，又不把解释权交出去？
hooks.text_en: **Once the rites are discarded, what marks a turning point**: graduation, divorce, redundancy, a death in the family, moving to a city where nobody knows you — such ruptures were once caught by ceremony and now mostly get a single post online. Fortune slips and birth charts may keep being invited back not because anyone believes the answer is written in the sky, but because they at least give the moment a form. So can a rite be built that carries no superstition — one that gives a turning point its shape without handing over the right to interpret it?
